### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 6  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.499)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-382556, Reactome:R-HSA-5678895, Reactome:R-HSA-9931269)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variants in ERLIN1 (MONDO:0014302) —DISRUPTS→ ERLIN1 (HGNC:27077); ERLIN1 (HGNC:27077) —DISRUPTS→ ER stress response (GO:0034976); ER stress response (GO:0034976) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Pathogenic variants in VCP (MONDO:0013501) —DISRUPTS→ VCP (HGNC:12304); VCP (HGNC:12304) —DISRUPTS→ Autophagosome-lysosome fusion (GO:0000287); Autophagosome-lysosome fusion (GO:0000287) —LEADS_TO→ Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (HP:0007240); Autophagosome-lysosome fusion (GO:0000287) —LEADS_TO→ Frontotemporal dementia (HP:0001249). Mutations in ERLIN1 (MONDO:0014302) disrupt ER stress response, leading to intellectual disability. Mutations in VCP (MONDO:0013501) disrupt autophagosome-lysosome fusion, leading to FTD/ALS. Both ER stress and impaired autophagy contribute to broader cellular proteostasis collapse.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that pathogenic variants in ERLIN1 do not impact ER stress response or that pathogenic variants in VCP do not affect autophagosome-lysosome fusion. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathways of protein homeostasis dysregulation in MONDO:0014302 and MONDO:0013501, mediated by ERLIN1 and VCP respectively, could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative diseases.

#### 2. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Y  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.491)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-382556, Reactome:R-HSA-5678895, Reactome:R-HSA-9931269)

Mutations in ERLIN1 disrupt the ER stress response, while mutations in VCP disrupt general protein homeostasis. Both pathways converge on a broader disruption of protein homeostasis, leading to the distinct phenotypes of MONDO:0014302 and CMT2Y.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any shared downstream cellular phenotypes related to ER stress or protein aggregation in cellular models derived from patients of both diseases, or identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways affected by ERLIN1 and VCP mutations respectively. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in ERLIN1 or VCP in the gnomAD database that do not segregate with either disease phenotype would weaken the hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream impact on protein homeostasis and ER stress could reveal common therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0014302 and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2Y, such as agents that enhance protein folding, clearance, or modulate the unfolded protein response.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of a gain-of-function mutation in VCP causative for either disease, or evidence that the VCP-associated myopathy, frontotemporal dementia, and Paget disease of bone phenotypes arise through completely independent molecular mechanisms not involving the ubiquitin-proteasome system. _(variant: The presence of common loss-of-function variants in VCP in the gnomAD database at a frequency greater than 1% would challenge the pathogenicity of these variants.)_

**How to falsify it:** The absence of any overlap in the functional consequences of ERLIN1 and PSMD12 mutations on ER stress response or proteasome function in cellular or animal models would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The identification of common, benign variants in ERLIN1 or PSMD12 in large control populations (e.g., gnomAD) that are also found in affected individuals would suggest alternative causal mechanisms.)_
